items.name: Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk")
items.summary: Mistral's largest and most capable model to date — a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal MoE (49B active parameters) trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Europe, targeting coding, agentic workflows, cybersecurity, finance and law. Available now as a public preview with open weights promised for end of October; Mistral claims it leads open-weight models built outside China.

items.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic's cheapest, fastest small model yet — built for high-volume tasks (classification, summarization, extraction, live support, voice agents) and as a subagent to Sonnet/Opus, at ~75% lower cost than Haiku 4.5. The first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting and built-in safeguards for high-risk cybersecurity requests.

items.name: Reflection AI Beam
items.summary: The first open-weight model from Nvidia-backed Reflection AI — a 501B-total/23B-active-parameter MoE aimed at coding and agentic tasks, positioned against Chinese open models like DeepSeek and Z.ai's GLM-5.2. The startup was founded in 2024 by ex-DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou.

items.name: Google Nano Banana 2.1
items.summary: Google's updated image generation and conversational-editing model (built on Gemini 3.6 Flash) with 1K/2K/4K outputs, multi-image fusion (up to 14 references), search grounding and stronger text rendering. Rolling out across the Gemini app, AI Studio, the Gemini API and Search AI Mode, with image API prices cut ~50% (a 1K image now costs $0.0336).

items.name: EmbeddingGemma 2
items.summary: Google DeepMind's open-weight (Apache 2.0) 740M-parameter multimodal embedding model that natively maps text, code, images, video and audio into a single 768-dim vector space — built for on-device search, classification and privacy-first RAG. Weights are live on Hugging Face and Kaggle with LiteRT/MediaPipe tooling.
